name: Loucetius

attributes.attribute: linked to healing at the shrine of Bath
seen as a form of Mars in Gaul

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Loucetius was a Celtic god worshipped in Gaul and Britain, also spelled Leucetius. He appears in a few inscriptions found in continental Gaul and in Britain. Loucetius was the consort of Nemetona, a goddess of sacred groves. A pair inscription was found at the healing shrine of Bath, which the Romans called Aquae Sulis, so Loucetius may have been a healing god. People in Gaul saw him as a form of Mars, the war god, and Mars could fight off disease. His name holds a syllable that means bright or shining, and scholars have read it as lightning.

okr.objective: Document the continental Celtic god Loucetius as a consort deity tied to healing and to Mars.
